items.bold: BRENT SURGED 6% to $118.03 Wednesday close — highest since April 7. Trump: "Choking like a stuffed pig."
items.text: CNBC (updated 9 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude futures rose about 6% to close at $118.03 — highest since early April. WTI futures advanced nearly 7% to $106.88. The surge came directly after Trump told Axios on Wednesday: "The blockade is somewhat more effective than the bombing. They are choking like a stuffed pig, and it is going to be worse for them. They can't have a nuclear weapon." This is the most explicit statement of Trump's war strategy — the blockade has replaced bombing as the primary weapon. For India: Brent $118 = OMC losses unsustainable, petrol/diesel hike of Rs 7-12/litre likely imminent — the largest consumer price shock of the war. India petroleum import bill at war-record levels.

items.bold: TRUMP DECLARED: Blockade continues UNTIL NUCLEAR DEAL. Hormuz-first deal explicitly ruled out.
items.text: CNBC confirmed Wednesday: Trump told Axios he will maintain the US naval blockade against Iran until they agree to a nuclear deal. This is a direct rejection of Iran's decoupled proposal (open Hormuz now, discuss nuclear later). Trump: "They can't have a nuclear weapon." Combined with Rubio's earlier statement that Iran's proposal is "unacceptable," this represents the clearest US position of the war: there is no Hormuz-first deal available. Nuclear must come first. The White House counterproposal, when delivered, will likely include this as a non-negotiable red line. For India: this means Hormuz stays blocked until a full nuclear deal is reached — which Al Jazeera analyst Mortazavi noted "took two years of intense negotiations" even under the more favourable Obama-era conditions.

items.bold: HEZBOLLAH LEADER flatly rejected all US-brokered Lebanon negotiations "and their outcomes."
items.text: CBS News (7 hours ago) confirmed: Hezbollah's leader has "flatly rejected the US-brokered negotiations between Israel and Lebanon 'and their outcomes,' raising new doubt over the tenuous ceasefire in the parallel war and further complicating prospects for a US-Iran deal." Hezbollah launched drones against IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon. Israel killed in combat in south Lebanon. CBS: "These incidents constitute a violation of the ceasefire understandings by the Hezbollah terrorist organization" (IDF statement). The Hezbollah rejection is significant for India because: Iran has consistently said it will not agree to any peace deal that does not also halt Israel's war in Lebanon. If Hezbollah explicitly rejects Lebanon negotiations, Iran has no pathway to a deal even if it wants one — it must first bring Hezbollah on board.

items.bold: US FED HELD RATES UNCHANGED — Powell's final meeting. Rupee gets partial relief.
items.text: Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged at Powell's final meeting as Fed Chair — as widely expected. Fed cited "elevated uncertainty from geopolitical conflict and energy prices." NPR confirmed. For India: Fed on hold = no additional dollar strength from rate hikes = partial rupee relief. The rupee had weakened to 94.81 intraday Wednesday on elevated oil and month-end dollar demand (The Week confirmed). A hawkish Fed surprise would have added to the rupee pressure — the hold provides some breathing room. However, Brent at $118 remains the dominant rupee pressure. India's trade deficit will widen significantly in April — highest petroleum import bill of the war. RBI may intervene in forex markets to defend the rupee if it approaches 96.

items.bold: IRAN REPORTEDLY LOST TRACK of Hormuz mines — cannot fully reopen even if it wants to.
items.text: CBS News (citing US officials) confirmed: Iran reportedly lost track of some mines it planted in the Strait of Hormuz, meaning it is "therefore unable to fully open the strait" even if it chose to. This is a critical structural fact — even an immediate deal does not mean immediate Hormuz reopening. US mine clearance operations are ongoing at "tripled level" per Trump's shoot-to-kill order, but Pentagon confirmed full clearance could take up to 6 months. Combined with tanker congestion (20,000+ mariners stranded, 2,000+ ships), production restart lags, and infrastructure damage — CNBC analyst Lipow: "even if hostilities ended immediately, oil markets take 4-6 months to stabilise." For India: Brent will not fall sharply to pre-war levels even on a deal day.

items.bold: LEBANON: 2,509+ killed. Hezbollah-Israel fighting intensifying despite ceasefire extension.
items.text: CBS News (7 hours ago) confirmed: At least 2,509 people have been killed in Lebanon since the war began (Lebanon health ministry). At least 3,375 killed in Iran (Iranian health authorities). Israel soldier killed in combat in south Lebanon Wednesday. Hezbollah "launched a number of explosive drones that detonated adjacent to IDF soldiers" — IDF confirmed no injuries. Hezbollah leader's rejection of all US-brokered negotiations "and their outcomes" effectively voids the Lebanon ceasefire framework. Israel maintains the right to pre-empt "immediate threats and even emerging threats" under ceasefire terms. Iran has said it will not agree to any deal without Lebanon ceasefire — and Hezbollah just rejected all Lebanon negotiations. This is a near-complete diplomatic deadlock.

items.bold: India Day 62: $118 Brent = Rs 7-12/L OMC hike imminent. Nuclear red line set. Fed on hold.
items.text: India-specific situation at 9:30 AM April 30: (1) Brent $118 = OMC petrol/diesel hike upgraded to Rs 7-12/L — most significant since the war began. Indian Oil, BPCL, HPCL announcement could come Thursday or Friday. (2) Trump's nuclear red line means no Hormuz reopening without a full nuclear deal — which could take months to years. (4) Hezbollah rejected Lebanon negotiations = Iran cannot agree to any deal even if it wants to — deepens the deadlock. (5) Iran lost track of Hormuz mines = even a deal today leaves Hormuz restricted for months. Today's open faces $118 Brent headwind.

assessment.body:
Thursday 9:30 AM IST. Day 62. The West Asia War entered its most economically destructive phase overnight.

THE NUCLEAR RED LINE — TRUMP CLOSES THE DOOR ON HORMUZ-FIRST
• Trump told Axios: "The blockade is somewhat more effective than the bombing."
• "They are choking like a stuffed pig, and it is going to be worse for them."
• "They can't have a nuclear weapon."
• WH: blockade continues UNTIL Iran agrees to nuclear deal
• Iran's decoupled Hormuz-first proposal is explicitly off the table
• The only path: full nuclear agreement first — then Hormuz reopening
• Last time Iran negotiated a nuclear deal: 2 years under Obama-era conditions

THE BRENT SHOCK — $118
• Brent +6% to $118.03 Wednesday close
• WTI +7% to $106.88
• Highest Brent since April 7 (near-peak of the oil shock)
• Triggered entirely by Trump's nuclear red line declaration
• For India: Rs 7-12/L petrol/diesel hike — IMMINENT

THE HEZBOLLAH VETO
• Hezbollah leader flatly rejected all US-brokered Lebanon negotiations
• Iran cannot agree to any deal without Lebanon ceasefire
• Hezbollah just made Lebanon ceasefire impossible
• Iran has no pathway to any deal — even if it wanted one
• Lebanon deaths: 2,509+ (steep climb)

THE MINES PROBLEM
• Iran reportedly lost track of mines planted in Hormuz
• Cannot fully reopen even if it wants to
• US mine clearing: 6 months even at "tripled level"
• Even a deal today = months of restricted transit
• Brent will not crash to pre-war levels even on a deal announcement

THE US FED — ONE POSITIVE
• Fed held rates unchanged (Powell's final meeting)
• Rupee gets partial relief — no additional dollar strength
• But Brent $118 overwhelms the Fed positive

INDIA AT DAY 62 — THE NEW REALITY
• Brent $118 = OMC hike Rs 7-12/L IMMINENT (Thursday-Friday)
• Kharif fertiliser: Hormuz now virtually certain to stay closed through June
• Emergency government action needed: alternate fertiliser suppliers
• Rupee 94.81 — approaching 95, RBI intervention possible
• Nuclear red line = India must plan for $110-120 Brent as new 2026 normal
• Sensex 77,496 (Apr 29 close) faces serious Thursday headwinds

VERDICT: Day 62 is the turning point. Trump has declared the blockade permanent until a full nuclear deal — and Hezbollah has simultaneously vetoed Iran's only exit ramp. Iran cannot open Hormuz (it lost its mines). It cannot make a deal (Hezbollah blocks Lebanon). And it is being strangled economically. This is no longer a war — it is a siege. And India, sitting downstream of every barrel that doesn't flow through Hormuz, is paying the highest price of any non-combatant nation.
